title: Restriction of the normalized proper compositor
statement:
Let $\ell$ be prime, let $E,F$ be finite extensions of $\mathbf Q_\ell$, and let $i:E\to F$ be a $\mathbf Q_\ell$-algebra homomorphism [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Put $A=\operatorname{ULift}(\mathcal O_E)$ and $B=\operatorname{ULift}(\mathcal O_F)$, and use $D_H(Z)=D(\operatorname{Fun}(\mathbf N^{\mathrm{op}},\operatorname{Mod}(\underline H_Z)))$ and its normalized operations $J_H,R_H$ [def-cbc-strict-constant-tower-operations]. Write $U_Z:D_B(Z)\to D_A(Z)$ for coefficient restriction and $o_j:U_ZJ_{A,j}\to J_{B,j}U_W$, $d_p:R_{B,p}U_T\to U_WR_{A,p}$ for openRestriction and properRestriction [def-pur-constant-scalar-tower-mates]. Write $P_Z^{(e)}$ for positive arithmetic selection of levels $e(n+1)$, $a_p:R_{B,p}P_T^{(e)}\to P_W^{(e)}R_{B,p}$ for reindexProper, and $b_j:J_{B,j}P_W^{(e)}\to P_Z^{(e)}J_{B,j}$ for reindexOpen [def-pur-strict-scalar-mate-evaluation-data]. Compositions of functors in these formulas are in execution order, as in Lean. Let $p:W\to T$, $g:T\to Y$ and $q:W\to Y$ be arbitrary scheme morphisms with $h:pg=q$. Let
$$t_H=\operatorname{rComp}_{H,p,g};\operatorname{eqToIso}(R_H(h)):R_{H,p}R_{H,g}\to R_{H,q}$$
be the normalized proper compositor followed by equality transport [def-cbc-strict-constant-tower-operations]. Then for every $M\in D_B(W)$,
$$R_{A,g}(d_p^{-1}(M));d_g^{-1}(R_{B,p}M);U_Y(t_B(M))=t_A(U_WM);d_q^{-1}(M).$$
For every $e\ge1$ and $M\in D_B(W)$,
$$P_Y^{(e)}(t_B(M));a_q(M)=a_g(R_{B,p}M);R_{B,g}(a_p(M));t_B(P_W^{(e)}M).$$
Here semicolon denotes arrows followed from left to right. These are identities of proper composition alone; there are no open immersions, compactifications or proper/open refinement arrows.

proof.text: On ordinary modules, the proper compositor restricts sections along the canonical iterated fibre-product isomorphism. Coefficient restriction keeps those sections and arithmetic selection keeps their indices. Hence both ordinary restriction squares commute with composition and transport along h.

Finite-free tensor is an exact left adjoint to coefficient restriction. Positive selection has the exact left adjoint supplied by arithmetic restriction resolution. Thus both preserve K-injectives. Derive the ordinary commuting squares on simultaneous whole-tower K-injective representatives. The normalized derived units identify them with properRestriction and reindexProper.

The canonical proper composition is normalized by the composite geometric adjunction. Its canonical derived-unit description agrees with that conjugate by uniqueness, so the derived ordinary compositor is exactly rComp. Naturality of normalized derived squares gives the two equations, retaining equality transport h.

lean.statement:
theorem strictProperCompositionRestriction
    {W T Y : Scheme.{u}} (p : W ⟶ T) (g : T ⟶ Y) (q : W ⟶ Y)
    (h : p ≫ g = q) :
    let A := ULift.{u + 1} (Padic.coefficientExtensionIntegers l E)
    let B := ULift.{u + 1} (Padic.coefficientExtensionIntegers l F)
    let tA := (rComp A p g).hom ≫ (eqToIso (congrArg (R A) h)).hom
    let tB := (rComp B p g).hom ≫ (eqToIso (congrArg (R B) h)).hom
    (∀ M : Derived B W,
      (R A g).map ((properRestriction l E F i p).inv.app M) ≫
          (properRestriction l E F i g).inv.app ((R B p).obj M) ≫
          (U l E F i Y).map (tB.app M) =
        tA.app ((U l E F i W).obj M) ≫ (properRestriction l E F i q).inv.app M) ∧
    ∀ (e : ℕ) (he : 1 ≤ e) (M : Derived B W),
      (subsequence l F Y e).map (tB.app M) ≫
          (reindexProper l F q e he).hom.app M =
        (reindexProper l F g e he).hom.app ((R B p).obj M) ≫
          (R B g).map ((reindexProper l F p e he).hom.app M) ≫
          tB.app ((subsequence l F W e).obj M)
